completion.alreadyInstalled: Tab completion is already set up in {files}.
completion.alreadyRemoved: {file} no longer holds the tab completion, so there was nothing to remove from it.
completion.bashPackage: Completion in bash also needs the bash-completion package. If it is not installed yet, install it with your system's package manager.
completion.bashProfile: On macOS, Terminal and iTerm open login shells, which read ~/.bash_profile and not {file}. If your ~/.bash_profile does not load {file} yet, add `source '{file}'` to it, or the block is never read.
completion.byHand: {file} already sets up tab completion for kurze-url, so it was left as it is.
completion.byHandLeft: {file} sets up tab completion for kurze-url without the marker `completion install` adds, so it was left as it is. Remove that setup by hand if you no longer want it.
completion.needsYes: There is no terminal to ask for confirmation. Add --yes to go ahead without asking.
completion.noHome: Could not find your home directory: {reason}
completion.noPowerShell: No PowerShell was found on the PATH.
completion.noShell: Could not tell which shell you use. Name it: `{command} SHELL`, where SHELL is one of {shells}.
completion.nothingToRemove: There is no tab completion set up by `completion install` in {files} to remove. For another shell, run `{command} SHELL`.
completion.policyBlocks: PowerShell's execution policy is {policy}, which keeps it from loading {file}, so completion stays off until the policy allows the profile to run. The policy was not changed.
completion.profileFailed: Could not ask {program} where its profile is: {reason}
completion.profileUnsafe: {file} is saved as UTF-16 or signed, and changing it from here would corrupt it or break its signature, so it was left as it is.
completion.reloadNewShell: Open a new shell to use it.
completion.reloadProfile: Open a new PowerShell window, or run `. '{file}'`, to use it.
completion.reloadSource: Open a new shell, or run `source '{file}'`, to use it.
completion.unknownShell: Tab completion can be set up for {shells}, not for “{shell}”. Name one of them: `{command} SHELL`.
